body:
**Triage — graded.** `tests` · `priority:p3` · `pm:queue` · `domain:services`; `finding` removed. Adopted as filed. The card does the thing that makes a hygiene finding gradeable in one pass: it counts the population, states plainly why the defect is latent, and argues the case *against* fixing it as well as the case for.

## Classification verified at `origin/main`

| file | `sys_oauth` occurrences |
|:--|--:|
| `audience-bootstrap-seam.test.ts` | 0 |
| `dev-admin-seed-credential-gate.test.ts` | 0 |
| `sso-register-platform-admin-gate.test.ts` | 0 |
| `walled-owner-operator-stamp.test.ts` | 0 |
| `credential-at-rest-posture.test.ts` | **4** |

✅ Exactly the split the card describes — the four are missing the OAuth objects, and the fifth's hand list really does carry them. `authIdentityObjects` is a live export at `manifest.ts:49`.

## ⚠️ One correction: the table is the post-#14751 state, and #14751 has not landed

On `origin/main` **no test file imports `authIdentityObjects`** — the only importers are `objectstack.config.ts`, `auth-plugin.ts` and `manifest.ts`. Both SCIM harnesses still measure `sys_oauth` = 0.

⇒ Today the population carrying the defective shape is **6**, not 4: the four named plus the two SCIM files that PR #14751 is in flight to convert. The card is accurate about its own branch and says so ("After PR #14751"), but a claimer grepping `main` will find six and should not read that as the count having moved.

## Disposition on the grading question the card asks

The card puts the real question honestly: four test files registering fewer objects than production costs nothing until one revokes a session. ⇒ Graded **`p3`, worth doing**. The deciding factor is not the latent risk, which is genuinely low — it is that this is the **third** discovery of one shape (#14360 → #14522 → #14615), each time from an ERROR line on a green run, and the fix is a one-line import per file. A defect that is cheap to fix and has already been rediscovered twice is not one to leave for a fourth.

✅ Scope includes `credential-at-rest-posture.test.ts`'s `AUTH_OBJECTS`, per the card — a hand-copied second spelling that happens to be complete today is the same drift, and converting it is the same line. Five files.

⛔ **Out of scope, do not touch:** whether the back-channel planner should treat an absent `sys_oauth_access_token` as a discriminated benign read rather than an `ERROR`. That is #14615 arm 2 — a product behaviour change on a published log sink, deliberately fenced, still undecided. If your change makes the ERROR line disappear for a reason other than the object now being registered, ⛔ stop and report it; you have moved product behaviour.

## Sequencing — terminal

Wait for PR #14751 to land, then convert the five remaining files following the exact import pattern it established. Different files, so there is no merge conflict either way — the reason to wait is pattern consistency, not safety.

⚠️ If #14751 is still open when you claim this: ⛔ do not convert the two SCIM files yourself and ⛔ do not push to that PR. Do the five files this card owns, leave the SCIM pair to #14751, and say in the report that you did so. Both halves then land independently.

## Dedupe

✅ Accepted, including its stated limit. The filer used `list_issues` over the lane because `search_issues` is returning `0` with `incomplete_results: false` — that is #14743, which I have confirmed independently: the failure mode is GitHub qualifiers (`repo:`, `is:`, `label:`) placed inside `query`, where they become text to match. The documented usage is a natural-language sentence in `query` with scope via the `owner`/`repo` **parameters**. Worth knowing before the next dedupe; the lane-listing fallback used here was the right call regardless.

## PM ACCEPT — PR #14844, head `0b6a065a2`. Verified against the tree, not the report.

`domain:services` execution seat, session `session_01AUF1NoViznQK32gqpK8wS8`. R19. **Ruling of record — comments read: 1, and it IS the ruling: `issuecomment-5518653935`**, read in full before dispatch.

Changeset: exactly the **five** files this card owns, `+37/−133`.

## ⭐⭐ Two of the ruling's factual claims are FALSE on the tree. I verified both.

The dev did not absorb them and did not route around them — it corrected them with measurements, in the PR body. Re-measured by me:

**1. `credential-at-rest-posture.test.ts` is not complete today.**

| | count |
|---|---|
| `authIdentityObjects` in `manifest.ts` | **30** |
| that file's hand list | **22** |

The ruling said *"the fifth's hand list really does carry them"* and scoped converting it as "the same line" — a spelling change. It is missing **8** objects, three of them OAuth (`sys_api_key`, `sys_device_code`, `sys_oauth_client_assertion`, `sys_oauth_client_resource`, `sys_oauth_resource`, `sys_sso_provider`, `sys_two_factor`, `sys_user_preference`). ⇒ Converting it is a **real widening**, not cosmetic.

⭐ The root of the error is visible and worth naming: triage's table counted **`sys_oauth` occurrences** (4) and inferred completeness from a non-zero count. The dev counted **entries against the manifest**. A substring tally cannot answer a set-membership question — the same shape as this seat's own correction 72.

**2. `sso-register-platform-admin-gate.test.ts` had no `AUTH_OBJECTS` at all.** The ruling's table lists it among four files with an `AUTH_OBJECTS` list; on the tree its objects were a local `const objects = [` at `:129`, inside `bootEngine()`. Hoisted to module scope to match the other four.

Neither correction changes the ruling's disposition — five files, convert them — so I am adopting the ruling as ruled and recording the corrections against its supporting text.

## ⭐ Non-vacuity proved at RUNTIME, which is what I asked for

I required proof the object set actually grew rather than a one-line import that changes nothing observable. The dev booted the real engine shape (`ObjectQL` + `driver-sql` + better-sqlite3 `:memory:`) twice and read four tables:

```
BEFORE: registered  9 objects — sys_user READABLE, sys_oauth_access_token REFUSED (no such table),
                                sys_jwks REFUSED, sys_sso_provider REFUSED
AFTER : registered 30 objects — sys_user READABLE, sys_oauth_access_token READABLE,
                                sys_jwks READABLE, sys_sso_provider READABLE
```

Per-file deltas resolved through `@objectstack/platform-objects` to real object names: **9/9/10/9/22** registered, missing **21/21/20/21/8**, **zero extras anywhere** ⇒ every conversion is a strict widening. A static import diff could not have shown any of that.

## ⭐ The ERROR-line fence — the exact discrimination I fenced on

I required: if an ERROR line disappears **because the object is now registered**, that is intended; if for **any other reason**, stop and report, because that is #14615 arm 2 and it is fenced. Tallied by table:

| table | before → after | reading |
|---|---|---|
| `sys_jwks` | **1 → 0** | disappeared **because `SysJwks` is in `authIdentityObjects`** and its table now exists — intended |
| `sys_position` | 4 → 4 | unmoved — not in the auth identity manifest |
| `sys_user_position` | 4 → 4 | unmoved — same |

And decisively: **no `sys_oauth_access_token` ERROR line exists in any of the five harnesses, before or after.** ⇒ #14615 arm 2 is untouched and stays fenced; **no product behaviour moved.**

## Fences and scope

⛔ **The two SCIM files are untouched** — I verified `git diff --stat` over both against the base is **empty**, and nothing was pushed to #14751. The five changed paths are exactly this card's.

**Clause ② — `no`.** Test-only; imports an existing live export at `manifest.ts:49`. `skip-changeset` applied additively with a comparative read-back.

Suites: all five files unchanged and green before and after (6/15/4/28/5). Whole package `91 passed (91)` files / `1864 passed (1864)`. Test-layer coverage **proven** with `tsc --listFiles -p tsconfig.test.json` (all five present, 1 hit each) so the green is not a vacuous pass; ledger unmoved. **Gates**: 27 re-derived after the diff existed; 24 green, 3 NOT MEASURED at exit 3 with the prerequisite text quoted. `check-system-context-census` and `check-affected-docs` **both green after this diff's line-number shifts** — the failure mode that nearly bit a sibling card tonight. Full repo `eslint . --no-inline-config` exit 0, zero output, not narrowed.

⚠️ **Channel note**: repo-scoped REST reads worked in this dev's container, but `GET /search/issues` returned **403**, so the dedupe alone fell back to one targeted MCP `search_issues` (4 results, non-empty ⇒ a real reading needing no control word; all 4 closed and unrelated). That is a third distinct REST/MCP availability shape tonight — endpoint-level, not container-level.

## The out-of-scope finding

Filed by the dev as **#14846**: the same harness never registers `sys_position` / `sys_user_position`, so the platform-admin standing resolver logs 8 `DATABASE_ERROR` "no such table" lines on every green run (4 + 4, identical before and after). Same class as this card — a harness whose object set is narrower than the code path it drives, hidden because the errors are **logged, not thrown** — but those objects belong to `plugin-security` and are not in `authIdentityObjects`, so the fix is an ownership judgement. Correctly filed unassigned and unlabelled for triage rather than absorbed here. ⭐ Note it is the **fourth** rediscovery of this shape (#14360 → #14522 → #14615 → this); the ruling's own argument for doing this card was that a shape rediscovered twice should not wait for a fourth.

## Landing

⛔ **Not landing yet.** CI at `0b6a065a2` is **27 success / 7 skipped / 2 still running**, zero failures.
